title: Coherent partition restriction diagram and its ind-Zariski presentation
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $P,S$ profinite spaces (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), and $g:\operatorname{Spec}R\to P$ and $f:S\to P$ continuous maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For each closed $Z\subseteq P$ let $R_Z$ be the canonical clopen-neighborhood colimit and use its canonical restriction maps as in [lem-pe-clopen-restriction-canonical-localization]. A finite clopen partition of $S$ is a finite set $\mathcal Q$ of nonempty pairwise disjoint clopen subsets with union $S$; for empty $S$ its partition is empty. Order the set $I$ of these partitions by refinement, $\mathcal Q\leq\mathcal Q'$ if every part of $\mathcal Q'$ lies in a part of $\mathcal Q$. Put
$$E_{\mathcal Q}=\prod_{A\in\mathcal Q}R_{f(A)}.$$
Each $f(A)$ is closed, $I$ is a small nonempty directed poset, and the maps whose $A'$-coordinate is projection to the containing $A$ followed by $R_{f(A)}\to R_{f(A')}$ form a diagram of commutative $R$-algebras on $I$. For fixed $\mathcal Q$, let $J_{\mathcal Q}$ be the product of the reverse-inclusion posets of clopen neighborhoods $U_A\supseteq f(A)$ in $P$. It is small nonempty directed, and the canonical comparison
$$\varinjlim_{(U_A)\in J_{\mathcal Q}}\prod_{A\in\mathcal Q}R[1/e_{U_A}]\ \longrightarrow\ E_{\mathcal Q}$$
is an $R$-algebra isomorphism, compatible with the coordinate localization maps; here $D(e_U)=g^{-1}(U)$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent]. Consequently $R\to E_{\mathcal Q}$ and $R\to\varinjlim_{\mathcal Q\in I}E_{\mathcal Q}$ are ind-Zariski: filtered colimits of finite products of principal localizations of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: First verify that each $f(A)$ is closed, without requiring $f$ to be open. Any open cover of the closed subset $A\subseteq S$, augmented by $S\setminus A$, covers compact $S$, so $A$ is compact. For $p\notin f(A)$ choose, for each $a\in A$, disjoint neighborhoods $O_a$ of $f(a)$ and $V_a$ of $p$ in Hausdorff $P$. The sets $A\cap f^{-1}(O_a)$ cover $A$; choose finitely many of them. The intersection of the corresponding $V_a$ is a neighborhood of $p$ missing $f(A)$. Thus $P\setminus f(A)$ is open.

source.place: Preliminaries: each f(A) is compact, hence closed; explicit finite-subcover argument.

proof.text: The partitions form a set, being finite subsets of the power set of $S$, and their refinement relation is a partial order. In fact, if two partitions refine each other, a part $A$ of the first is contained in a part $B$ of the second and then in a part $A_1$ of the first; nonemptiness and disjointness force $A=A_1$, hence $A=B$. For $S\ne\varnothing$ the partition $\{S\}$ exists, and for $S=\varnothing$ the empty partition exists. The nonempty intersections $A\cap B$ of parts of two partitions give a finite clopen partition refining both. Thus $I$ is small, nonempty and directed, and therefore filtered.

For a refinement $\mathcal Q\leq\mathcal Q'$, every $A'\in\mathcal Q'$ lies in a unique $A\in\mathcal Q$. Since $f(A')\subseteq f(A)$ are closed, the canonical restriction lemma supplies the $R$-algebra map $r_{A,A'}:R_{f(A)}\to R_{f(A')}$. Define $t_{\mathcal Q,\mathcal Q'}$ by $\operatorname{pr}_{A'}t_{\mathcal Q,\mathcal Q'}=r_{A,A'}\operatorname{pr}_A$. The product ring operations make this an $R$-algebra map. Identity restrictions are identities, since their neighborhood-diagram inclusions are identities. For a further refinement with $A''\subseteq A'\subseteq A$, the restriction lemma gives $r_{A',A''}r_{A,A'}=r_{A,A''}$. Hence the refinement maps satisfy identity and composition in every coordinate and define the claimed diagram.

source.place: Tag 097D, lemma-construct-profinite: transition maps; blueprint Preliminaries made canonical using Tag 097C.

proof.text: Fix $\mathcal Q$. In each coordinate the clopen neighborhoods of $f(A)$ form the small nonempty directed poset supplied by the canonical restriction lemma. More explicitly, $P$ is a neighborhood and intersection is an upper bound in reverse inclusion. The finite product $J_{\mathcal Q}$ is a set, has the tuple $(P)_A$, and two tuples have the coordinatewise-intersection upper bound. Its transition maps on $B_{\mathbf U}:=\prod_A R[1/e_{U_A}]$ are the coordinate localization maps from that lemma. They compose coordinatewise. The coordinate colimit coprojections $\iota_{A,U}:R[1/e_U]\to R_{f(A)}$ give compatible product maps $b_{\mathbf U}:B_{\mathbf U}\to E_{\mathcal Q}$. The small-colimit existence theorem gives $L_{\mathcal Q}=\varinjlim_{\mathbf U\in J_{\mathcal Q}}B_{\mathbf U}$, and the colimit universal property gives the unique $R$-algebra comparison $c:L_{\mathcal Q}\to E_{\mathcal Q}$ with $c\lambda_{\mathbf U}=b_{\mathbf U}$.

proof.text: Apply the source-library instance IsIPC for CommAlgCat R. It transfers the IPC property of Type along the forgetful functor, which preserves products and filtered colimits and reflects isomorphisms. The canonical colimitPointwiseProductToProductColimit is therefore an isomorphism, including for the empty product. Its coordinate equation is Mathlib ι_colimitPointwiseProductToProductColimit_π. No new representative or eventual-equality proof is required.

For each neighbourhood tuple, identify its categorical product with the type-theoretic product using CommAlgCat.isLimitPiFan and enumerate its finite quotient-point index by Fin n. Each factor is literally Localization.Away at the pulled-back clopen idempotent. This gives a principal-block filtered presentation of the colimit of the neighbourhood diagram. Transport it across the specified comparison isomorphism by ObjectProperty.ind.prop_of_iso to obtain the partition-stage assertion. Fin 0 handles the empty partition.

Define D on the prescribed products with each new coordinate equal to projection to its parent followed by refinementRestriction. Prove its laws by Pi.hom_ext and quotient induction: on a representative s all parent points are the quotient class of s, so restriction_naturality supplies identity and composition. The displayed coordinate equation is Pi.lift_π. This retains the prescribed coherent refinement diagram.

Let blocks be the property of being algebra-isomorphic to a finite product of principal localizations. Such products are etale and hence finitely presented. CommRingCat.isFinitelyPresentable_under proves finite presentability in Under R; isCardinalPresentable_iff_of_isEquivalence transfers it to CommAlgCat R. Apply ObjectProperty.ind_ind to blocks. The colimit presentation of D with its already proved ind-block objects exhibits its colimit in blocks.ind.ind, and idempotence gives blocks.ind, precisely IsIndPrincipalZariski. This is a direct proof of the fixed-base filtered-colimit clause, without the general arrow-category stability theorem.

The existential functor has literal prescribed product objects (hD) and all transition coordinates fixed to canonical restrictions; it is not an unspecified diagram.
